forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {治|なお}していませんでした

definitions.gloss: to cure; to heal; to remedy
definitions.explanation: To restore someone to health by treating a disease or injury. The subject is the person or thing doing the healing (a doctor, medicine, etc.).

examples.japanese: ⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}した。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{薬|くすり}→薬：00793_kusuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{風邪|かぜ}→風邪：02188_kaze⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}すこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: You can cure a cold with this medicine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{虫歯|むしば}→虫歯：00299_mushiba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{早|はや}め→早め：11176_hayame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{歯医者|はいしゃ}→歯医者：01696_haisha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{治|なお}した⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: It's better to have cavities treated at the dentist early on.

notes:
This is the medical/healing なおす, written with {治|なお}す. It means to cure illness or heal injury, as opposed to {直|なお}す which means to fix or repair broken objects or mistakes. Both are read なおす but use different kanji.

CONTRAST WITH {直|なお}す:
- {治|なお}す — to cure/heal (illness, injury)
- {直|なお}す — to fix/repair (broken objects, mistakes)

INTRANSITIVE PAIR:
- {治|なお}す (transitive) — someone cures something
- ⟦{治|なお}る→治る：19598_naoru⟧ (intransitive) — something heals/gets better on its own

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}す — to cure an illness
- {怪我|けが}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}す — to heal an injury
- ⟦{虫歯|むしば}→虫歯：00299_mushiba⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}す — to treat a cavity
- ⟦{風邪|かぜ}→風邪：02188_kaze⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{治|なお}す — to cure a cold
